selected.comparison: Linear latent-variable baseline on lightly smoothed, mean-centered spectra; only latent count varies, so the run isolates the effect of noise suppression versus the tiny 8-band dimension.

decisions.rationale: Round 1 should be a low-variance, interpretable probe rather than an expensive nonlinear search. PLS with a 3-value latent grid on lightly SG-smoothed, mean-centered spectra costs 16 fits, leaves 2 experiments, and directly tests the dominant profile tag (high-frequency noise) while keeping the pipeline simple enough that round 2 remains diagnosable. n_components is the single most consequential free parameter for 8 collinear bands, so it is the only grid dimension.
decisions.expected_outcome: A trained PLS on SG-smoothed mean-centered Cal spectra returning Cal CV RMSE and Validation RMSE/R2; expected a modest, interpretable linear fit whose residuals indicate whether round 2 should pursue SNV+derivative scatter correction (alternative B) or a non-linear family (C/D).

expected_improvement.text_expectation: A trained PLS on SG-smoothed mean-centered Cal spectra returning Cal CV RMSE and Validation RMSE/R2; expected a modest, interpretable linear fit whose residuals indicate whether round 2 should pursue SNV+derivative scatter correction (alternative B) or a non-linear family (C/D).

alternatives.comparison: Linear latent-variable baseline on lightly smoothed, mean-centered spectra; only latent count varies, so the run isolates the effect of noise suppression versus the tiny 8-band dimension.

Scatter/baseline-focused linear alternative: SNV plus first derivative should remove additive/multiplicative scatter and slow drift before a shrunk linear model, testing the scatter_variation tag more directly than smoothing alone.
Non-linear kernel alternative with minimal preprocessing, exploring whether the protein response is non-linear; risky with n=36 and only 8 bands, hence a deliberately small 2-candidate grid.
Tree-ensemble alternative to test non-linearity and band interactions without internal scaling; fixed depth bounds variance on a 36-sample Cal set.

proposal.difference: First experiment of the session: no persisted experiments exist. This direction establishes a PLS baseline on the 8-wavelength Cal set with light SG smoothing plus mean centering, chosen to probe whether the flagged high-frequency noise (score 0.739) is a real limitation before spending fits on fancier families/preprocessing.
proposal.expected_outcome: A trained PLS on SG-smoothed mean-centered Cal spectra returning Cal CV RMSE and Validation RMSE/R2; expected a modest, interpretable linear fit whose residuals indicate whether round 2 should pursue SNV+derivative scatter correction (alternative B) or a non-linear family (C/D).
hypotheses: Because the Cal profile flags high-frequency noise, light SG smoothing (window 7, order 2) should reduce Cal CV RMSE relative to raw spectra without erasing the broad protein absorption bands.
With only 8 collinear bands, a low latent count (1-3) should be sufficient; the CV objective should pick a small n_components rather than overfitting the 36 Cal samples.

If a smoothed PLS baseline already explains most Cal variance, more complex families (SVR/ET) will not be needed; otherwise residuals will guide round 2 toward scatter correction or a non-linear family.

not_selected_reasons.B_ridge_snv_deriv: Not selected first: derivative-based scatter correction is a larger transformation on only 8 bands and would confound the baseline read; SNV+derivative is deferred to round 2 if the smoothed linear fit leaves systematic structure.
not_selected_reasons.C_svr_raw_rbf: Not selected first: RBF SVR is the most hyperparameter-sensitive option and n=36 with 8 bands gives little margin to exploit non-linearity; deferred unless Cal/Val residuals show clear curvature.
not_selected_reasons.D_et_sgsmooth: Not selected first: fixed trees are less interpretable and typically need more samples to beat a regularized linear model on this dimension; deferred as a non-linearity check.

observations.claim: Calibration set has 36 samples and only 8 wavelengths (900-1600 nm), target protein in % spans -4.93 to 3.29 with std 2.12; the very wide target spread relative to a small sample count makes over-parameterized models risky.

The Cal profile is tagged high_frequency_noise, low_signal_to_noise and scatter_variation, with high_frequency_noise_score=0.7393, scatter_variation_score=0.2483, baseline_drift_score=0.1490; these are descriptive proxies only and do not establish causes or mandate preprocessing.

Evaluation is a sealed holdout: selection is on the 12-sample Validation set and Test is accessible only after an explicit freeze; CV is frozen 5-fold KFold on the 36 Cal samples with objective train_cv_rmse.

PLS is an applicable linear latent-variable comparator for quantitative, collinear NIR data; the project adapter uses scale=False and selects components within training, with n_components writable in 1-20.

Savitzky-Golay smoothing is applicable where high-frequency noise is present and wide absorption bands should be preserved; the project adapter supports odd windows 5-15 and polynomial order 1-4, with 7/11/15 as candidates and no official optimum.
Budget is 3 experiments / 18 total fits; a fixed pipeline still costs 6 fits (5 CV + 1 full-Cal refit), so each of the three experiments can afford a small grid of at most 3 candidates.

proposal.rationale: Round 1 should be a low-variance, interpretable probe rather than an expensive nonlinear search. PLS with a 3-value latent grid on lightly SG-smoothed, mean-centered spectra costs 16 fits, leaves 2 experiments, and directly tests the dominant profile tag (high-frequency noise) while keeping the pipeline simple enough that round 2 remains diagnosable. n_components is the single most consequential free parameter for 8 collinear bands, so it is the only grid dimension.
uncertainties: Whether the high high_frequency_noise_score genuinely reflects noise in the spectra or is an artifact of the small 8-band axis; smoothing may add little if the noise is mostly low-level.
How representative the 12-sample Validation set is; a single small holdout can be noisy, so I will also weigh the 5-fold Cal CV alongside Val metrics.
Whether the wide target range (-4.93 to 3.29) is genuine chemistry or contains heteroscedastic/outlier samples that will dominate RMSE.
